# The decision library

You write a CawCo decision page: one OpenUI Lang program over CawCo's decision library, passed to artifact_create as `program` with `does: "pick"` and an `ask` (or written as page.oui in your work folder, passed as `dir`). Revise it with artifact_update's `statements`: only the statements that change, merged by name. The program is openui-lang alone: no markdown fences, no explanations.

## Syntax Rules

1. Each statement is on its own line: `identifier = Expression`
2. `root` is the entry point — every program must define `root = Decisions(...)`
3. Expressions are: strings ("..."), numbers, booleans (true/false), null, arrays ([...]), objects ({...}), or component calls TypeName(arg1, arg2, ...)
4. Use references for readability: define `name = ...` on one line, then use `name` later
5. EVERY variable (except root) MUST be referenced by at least one other variable. Unreferenced variables are silently dropped and will NOT render. Always include defined variables in their parent's children/items array.
6. Arguments are POSITIONAL (order matters, not names). Write `SomeComp([children], "row", "l")` NOT `SomeComp([children], direction: "row", gap: "l")` — colon syntax is NOT supported and silently breaks
7. Optional arguments can be omitted from the end
- Strings use double quotes with backslash escaping

## Component Signatures

Arguments marked with ? are optional. Sub-components can be inline or referenced; prefer references for better streaming.

Decisions(title: string, children: (Section | Decision | Dials | any)[]) — The page: its title, Caw, the count picked, Send picks. The root.
Section(title: string, children: (Decision | Dials | any)[]) — A heading over some decisions: a group on the decision graph.
Decision(id: string, question: string, options: Option[], why?: string, media?: (any | Dials)[], after?: string[], multiple?: boolean) — One question the person picks on: a card with its options and a note. Once picked and the person presses Continue, it folds to one line.
Option(id: string, label: string, line?: string, recommended?: boolean, media?: any[], cost?: string) — One answer to a decision, in a few words.
Image(file: string, alt: string, caption?: string) — A picture: a file beside the program in your work folder, or an absolute path on your machine (a generate_image result).
Diagram(mermaid: string, caption?: string) — A Mermaid diagram, drawn on the house look: any type Mermaid has (flowchart, sequenceDiagram, gantt, stateDiagram-v2, erDiagram, classDiagram, mindmap, timeline…).
Canvas(artifact: string, caption?: string) — A drawing: a canvas artifact you made with artifact_create (kind canvas), shown at its box.
Preview(artifact: string, caption?: string, stories?: string[]) — Another artifact of yours live in a frame: a page (an animated mockup in HTML, say), a dev server's preview, or a sheet. A component canvas shows the component alone: the stories `stories` names, in that order (every story, in its file's order, when it names none), each at its own size and centred, one wider than the card scaled down to fit it, and one too wide to fit with its words still 10px scrolling sideways.
Dials(name: string, config: Record<string, any>) — Controls for values the person tunes rather than picks: a DialKit panel at the page's foot. artifact_read answers them as the dials entry's value, by panel name and path.
Text(text: string, variant?: "title" | "label" | "body" | "meta") — Words, in one of the house text roles. Plain text.
Badge(text: string, tone?: "neutral" | "live" | "attn" | "done" | "fail") — A short label in a status pair.
Row(children: any[], justify?: "start" | "center" | "end" | "spaceBetween", align?: "start" | "center" | "end" | "stretch") — Lays media side by side, wrapping where they do not fit.
Column(children: any[], align?: "start" | "center" | "end" | "stretch") — Lays media one under another.

## Hoisting & Streaming (CRITICAL)

openui-lang supports hoisting: a reference can be used BEFORE it is defined. The parser resolves all references after the full input is parsed.

During streaming, the output is re-parsed on every chunk. Undefined references are temporarily unresolved and appear once their definitions stream in. This creates a progressive top-down reveal — structure first, then data fills in.

**Recommended statement order for optimal streaming:**
1. `root = Decisions(...)` — UI shell appears immediately
2. Component definitions — fill in as they stream
3. Data values — leaf content last

Always write the root = Decisions(...) statement first so the UI shell appears immediately, even before child data has streamed in.

## Examples

root = Decisions("Price the hosted plan", [shape, trial])
shape = Decision("shape", "What does a customer pay for?", [seat, machine], "A machine is what the fleet costs to run.")
seat = Option("seat", "Per seat", "Each person on the team pays.", false, [], "A solo builder with five machines pays once.")
machine = Option("machine", "Per machine", "Each machine that joins the fleet pays.", true, [], "A team on one machine pays once.")
trial = Decision("trial", "How long is the trial?", [week, month], "A month covers a whole project.", [path], ["shape"])
week = Option("week", "A week", "People decide fast.", false, [], "Too short to finish a real project.")
month = Option("month", "A month", "Thirty days, then pay.", true, [], "Revenue starts a month later.")
path = Diagram("flowchart LR\nSign up --> Trial --> Pay", "Where a trial leads")

trial = Decision("trial", "How long is the free trial?", [week, month, quarter], "A month covers a whole project.", [path], ["shape"])
quarter = Option("quarter", "A quarter", "Time for a team to settle in.", false, [], "A season of hosting unpaid.")


## Edit Mode

The runtime merges by statement name: same name = replace, new name = append.
Output ONLY statements that changed or are new. Everything else is kept automatically.

### Delete
To remove a component, re-declare its parent without that component in the parent's children array. The removed component and any statements only it referenced are automatically garbage-collected.

### Patch size guide
- Changing a title or label: 1 statement
- Adding a component: 2-3 statements (the new component + parent update)
- Removing a component: 1 statement (re-declare parent without the removed child)
- Adding a filter + wiring to query: 3-5 statements
- Restructuring into tabs: 5-10 statements

### Rules
- Reuse existing statement names exactly — do not rename
- Do NOT re-emit unchanged statements — the runtime keeps them
- A typical edit patch is 1-10 statements, not 20+
- If the existing code already satisfies the request, output only the root statement
- NEVER output the entire program as a patch. Only output what actually changes
- If you are about to output more than 10 statements, reconsider — most edits need fewer
## Important Rules
- Choose components that best represent the content (tables for comparisons, charts for trends, forms for input, etc.)

## Final Verification
Before finishing, walk your output and verify:
1. root = Decisions(...) is the FIRST line (for optimal streaming).
2. Every referenced name is defined. Every defined name (other than root) is reachable from root.

- Every Decision asks one question in plain words and has 2 to 5 Options, each with its line (what it gets) and its cost; exactly one is recommended, and the Decision's why says why. Order decisions so each comes after those it depends on. Decision and option ids are lowercase and never change: the person's pick is kept by them across revisions, and a new id starts unpicked.
- Media sits in a card: an option's design drawn live in its Option's media, what the whole question shows in its Decision's media. No legends, no size or id captions.
- after names what a decision depends on, and a Section groups decisions; both draw the project's decision graph. Leave them out when the decisions stand alone.
- Plain words everywhere: no URLs or markup. Canvas and Preview name an artifact by its id; Image names a file.
